description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/lib.rs:292

  pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler;

This re-export sits at the bottom of lib.rs, after the
register_chat_handlers function body, with no documentation. It
looks like a paste-in convenience for closure-shaped handler
registration in downstream code.

Effect on the contract:

1. jmap-chat-server's public API surface is now tied to
   jmap_server::ClosureHandler. If jmap-server cuts a major
   version that reshapes ClosureHandler (rename, generic-param
   change, new associated type), jmap-chat-server is broken at
   the same major bump — even if jmap-chat-server itself made no
   changes.

2. The workspace's path-dep convention (jmap-chat-server depends
   on jmap-server via `path = '../crate-jmap-server'`) makes the
   coupling invisible until the first release. The day someone
   publishes to crates.io and jmap-server cuts a 0.x → 0.y, every
   consumer pinning ^0.x of jmap-chat-server breaks unless they
   also bump jmap-server.

3. No rustdoc on the re-export. A consumer browsing the docs sees
   ClosureHandler appear in jmap-chat-server's exports but no
   explanation of why or what it's for.

Workspace AGENTS.md API-contract section ('Versioning and
deprecation' / 'Implementation leakage'):

  'Re-exports from upstream crates that lock the major version.
   If you pub use foo::Bar and foo cuts a major version, your
   crate's API is broken too. Either re-export through your own
   newtype or document the upstream version pin.'

Fix options:

A. (Likely correct) Delete the line. register_chat_handlers
   builds the ClosureHandler internally via the reg! macro;
   consumers do not need to construct one themselves. If a
   consumer needs ClosureHandler for their own
   non-chat-server-managed handler, they already depend on
   jmap-server (it's the dispatcher source) and can import it
   from there.

B. Keep the re-export and document the upstream major-version
   coupling in the lib.rs doc:
     'jmap-chat-server's MSRV/major-version is pinned to
     jmap-server's; bump them together.'

C. Wrap in a newtype:
     pub struct ClosureHandler<C>(jmap_server::ClosureHandler<C>);

   …with re-implemented constructor + Deref. Overkill for a
   minor convenience.

A is the minimum-change correct fix.
title: API contract: pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler leaks upstream major version
